messages:
maya: heads-up — canary for 13B-AWQ with act-quant enabled started showing higher decode entropy and hallucination rate after ~2h in Dedicated pool. small sample eval on wikitext/gqa shows +6% perplexity and some factual mismatches :confused:

maya: repro steps: rolled model AWQ-gptj-13b v2 -> group_size=64, act_quant=per_channel, warmstart cache on. traffic routed 10% canary via smart-routing policy.

maya: sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T15:23:41Z] decode_entropy=4.8 -> 6.1
[2026-03-17T15:24:02Z] generated: "The founder died in 2009"  (ground truth: 2019)
```

tom: ugh. did we change KV cache eviction or prefix caching recently?

maya: nope, prefix cache unchanged. but I noticed a correlation with group-size bursts — when group collapses to 1/2 the configured batching (spikes) entropy jumps.

ethan: can you paste eval diffs? a quick table is fine.

maya: quick numbers from our smoke eval (50 prompts, deterministic seed):
- fp16 baseline: bleu=23.4, ppl=12.1
- awq (g64, act=per_chan): bleu=20.1, ppl=12.9
- awq (g32, act=per_chan): bleu=22.6, ppl=12.3
- awq (g64, act=none): bleu=23.0, ppl=12.2

maya: so two knobs look most relevant — group_size and act_quant. flipping act quant off largely restores quality, lowering group_size helps too.

tom: interesting. that suggests act-quant interacts with batching-induced activation distributions. maybe quantization scales were computed on short prefixes and break with varied batch ordering.

ethan: yeah — AWQ's per-channel act quant relies on activation statistics. if runtime batching changes the distribution (different sequence lengths / padding), scale mismatch can occur.

priya: deploy-bot reports: canary traffic at 10% -> 14:45 UTC saw spike to 25% due to retry storm, then we had a small surge. could that have expanded group-size variance?

maya: exactly — surge increased variance in group composition (many short/long mixes). i repro'd locally by replaying that traffic mix and saw identical entropy jump.

lucas: is this consistently reproducible on Hosted or only Dedicated?

maya: reproducible on Dedicated pools with our current batching policy. Hosted (multi-tenant) didn't show the same effect in quick checks — likely different batching heuristics.

tom: mitigation plan suggestions:
1) short-term: set act_quant=none for this model and reduce group_size to 32 for the canary.
2) medium-term: recompute activation scales with traffic-shaped calibration (include varied seq length batches).
3) longer-term: runtime-aware per-request scaling fallback and a small prefix-cache bypass for quantized layers.

maya: i've already pushed a hotfix to canary: act_quant=none, group_size=32. monitoring now.

deploy-bot: rollout update: canary config patched at 1762500067, traffic remains 10% until stability OK.

ethan: nice. when we revert act-quant we lose most of the AWQ memory/cost win though — any perf numbers?

maya: perf impact — token throughput down ~8%, mem up ~12% vs awq+act. still below fp16 baseline in mem but closer.

lucas: for the calibration job, I can spin a traffic-shaped sampler that mirrors the surge mix. we should include tail-latency heavy sequences.

maya: please do. also we should add a small unit test in awq integration: simulate mixed-length batches and verify no >3% BLEU drop vs baseline.

priya: tagging on-call infra: @tom @lucas please monitor Dedicated queue latencies for next 3 hours, will escalate if errors >0.5% or hallucination alerts pop. :eyes:

tom: will watch. thanks for quick fix, maya.

maya: i'll follow up with PR that adds 'traffic-shaped calibration' to our onboarding checklist, and add a note in the model card about act-quant sensitivity to batch composition.

ethan: also let's capture a small experiment run with fp8-like emulation vs awq to see if lower-bit backoffs help.

maya: ack — scheduling calibration runs and will post results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
